about: Where each true-to-life Bio view comes from: what it shows, the real preparation it must match, the measurable facts the drawing encodes with the code that sets them, public references to compare against, and a sign-off block for a reviewer. How to sign off: docs/bio-visual-references.md.
lines: Each code location gives the file, the line and match, a regular expression for that line. tests/bio/stick-cards.test.js checks on every npm test that match still sits on the cited line; if a drawing file changes, the test names the line it moved to.

statuses.matches: Inside the real range given, or the same in kind for a fact without a number.
statuses.close: A little outside the real range, or right in kind but not in number. Listed so the reviewer judges it first; the reason says why.
statuses.deviates: Outside the real range by enough to notice in a side-by-side look. The reason says why it was left.

verification.seen-in-search: The URL appeared in a web search result on 2026-10-30. The page itself was not opened from the build sandbox, so check that it loads and check the license on the page.
verification.not-verified: The citation is from memory or the URL follows the publisher pattern; it was not seen. Check it before relying on it.

references.title: Cell Image Library CIL:10817, mouse skeletal muscle, longitudinal TEM (from The Cell, Fawcett)
references.license: CC BY-NC-ND per the CIL page (another record lists it as under copyright); view only
references.use: Band pattern, Z discs and mitochondria in a longitudinal section. Its prep is osmium-ferrocyanide, not the uranyl acetate and lead citrate the TEM records ask for: the T tubules and the space outside the cell are dark and the SR is unstained, so it places the T tubules (two per sarcomere, at the A-I junctions) but does not show whole triads. For triads, use cil-10815, columbia-muscle-em or skm-2011-triad.

views.view: Tonicity: red blood cells under the light microscope

open.steps: Tonicity and Osmosis Sandbox: tap "Animal cell (no wall)", then set External solute to 50.

views.depicts: Human red blood cells in an isotonic solution: round biconcave discs with a pale center, a few touching, one overlapping pair, two seen edge-on. No nucleus.
views.mustMatch: Unstained wet mount of human red blood cells, brightfield, 1000x oil immersion, camera crop.

facts.fact: Disc diameter 7.5 um
facts.real: Normal red cells are about 7 to 8 um across

code.sets: red cell radius 21 px at 5.6 px per um, so a disc is 7.5 um across

facts.fact: Edge-on profile 1.0 um thick at the center and 2.7 um at the thickest (the Evans and Fung shape with a 1.0 um center term)
facts.real: Evans and Fung mean cell: 7.8 um across, 0.81 um at the center, 2.58 um at the thickest (plus or minus about 0.3 um from cell to cell)
facts.reason: The center term is 1.0 um instead of the measured 0.81 um, so the drawn cell is 0.2 um thicker at the center and 0.12 um thicker at the thickest (2.70 against 2.58 um). Both are inside the cell-to-cell spread.

code.sets: edge-on thickness profile: (1 + 7.83 c^2 - 4.39 c^4) um, times the sine of the angle

facts.fact: Central pallor about one third of the diameter, near-even rim
facts.real: Pallor about one third of the diameter

code.sets: disc color stops: pale center to 30 percent, rim from 42 percent

facts.fact: 34 cells in a 66 x 41 um field; 2 edge-on, 1 overlapping pair
facts.real: A wet mount shows cells at random: some touch or overlap, a few edge-on

code.sets: cell layout [x, y, size, roundness, tilt, flag]

facts.fact: Scale bar 10 um = 56 px
facts.real: Scale bar must match the drawing

code.sets: scale bars: 10 um = 56 px for red cells, 50 um = 60 px for Elodea

facts.fact: Isotonic for external solute 46 to 54 (cell = 50)
facts.real: No net water flow

code.sets: isotonic band: external solute within 5 of the cell (50)

simplified: Color is a soft salmon, between a stained smear and an unstained wet mount.
No rouleaux (stacks) are drawn.

views.view: Tonicity: red blood cells under the light microscope

open.steps: Tonicity and Osmosis Sandbox: tap "Animal cell (no wall)", set External solute to 32 (cups), then 18 (spheres).

views.depicts: Water enters: the discs first cup (stomatocytes, the pallor narrows to a slit), then round up into evenly dense spheres that hold more water yet look a little narrower.
views.mustMatch: Unstained wet mount of human red blood cells in hypotonic saline, brightfield, 1000x oil.

facts.fact: Sphere diameter shrinks to about 6.7 um (radius x (1 - 0.11 t))
facts.real: The membrane barely stretches, so the swollen sphere is narrower than the disc (about 6.5 to 7 um)

code.sets: swollen radius

facts.fact: Cup stage: slit-shaped pallor up to 0.45 x 0.12 of the radius, shown while 0.2 < t < 0.7
facts.real: Stomatocytes show a slit-like central pallor

code.sets: slit pallor

facts.fact: Lysis starts below external solute 12 (a quarter of the cell, 50)
facts.real: Red cells start to lyse near half the isotonic concentration (about 0.45 percent NaCl against 0.9) and are all lysed near a third (about 0.3 percent)
facts.reason: The sandbox scale is relative, and its lysis waits for a quarter of the cell value where real cells begin near a half; the cups (32) and spheres (18) also sit lower than in real cells. The order of the states is right. A picture-level review will not see this; it matters only if the numbers are taught.

code.sets: lysis threshold

simplified: Swelling is shown as one smooth sequence; real cells differ in when they cup and round up.

views.view: Tonicity: red blood cells under the light microscope

open.steps: Tonicity and Osmosis Sandbox: tap "Animal cell (no wall)", then set External solute to 4.

views.depicts: Cells have burst: faint, smooth, empty membranes (ghosts) about the size of the spheres in an evenly tinted, nearly empty field. At external solute 8 to 11, two tougher cells still hold as spheres.
views.mustMatch: Brightfield wet mount after hypotonic hemolysis, 1000x oil (ghosts are hard to see without phase contrast).

facts.fact: Ghost diameter 6.75 um (0.9 of the disc), smooth outline, fill opacity 0.12
facts.real: Ghosts reseal at about 6 to 7 um and are nearly invisible in brightfield
facts.reason: The size matches. The ghosts are drawn a little easier to see than in true brightfield, on purpose (see simplified).

code.sets: ghost circle

facts.fact: Released hemoglobin tints the whole field faintly (opacity 0.15)
facts.real: The tube looks clear red; the thin layer under the microscope is only faintly tinted

code.sets: field tint

facts.fact: Two cells hold as spheres at external solute 8 to 11
facts.real: Cells differ in osmotic fragility

code.sets: tougher cells

simplified: Ghosts are drawn a little more visible than true brightfield so the student can find them.

open.steps: Tonicity and Osmosis Sandbox: tap "Animal cell (no wall)", then set External solute to 92.

views.depicts: Water leaves: shrunken cells with many short, blunt, evenly spaced projections over the rim and the face (echinocytes), only a little darker than normal cells.

views.view: Tonicity: Elodea leaf cells under the light microscope

open.steps: Tonicity and Osmosis Sandbox: tap "Plant cell (rigid wall)", then set External solute to 50.

views.depicts: Elodea leaf cells in parallel files, thin colorless walls, colorless cytoplasm packed with chloroplasts along the walls and over the face; in about half the cells the membrane just starts to leave the corners (incipient plasmolysis).
views.mustMatch: Wet mount of an Elodea (Egeria) leaf, brightfield, 400x, camera crop.

facts.fact: Scale 1.2 px per um; scale bar 50 um = 60 px
facts.real: Scale bar must match the drawing

code.sets: scale bars: 10 um = 56 px for red cells, 50 um = 60 px for Elodea

facts.fact: Cells 30 um wide and 77 to 125 um long, in files
facts.real: Class measurements give about 20 to 30 um wide and 60 to 130 um long (acadia-elodea), with a typical cell about 50 x 25 um (exploratorium-elodea); size varies with the leaf and the place in it
facts.reason: Inside the wider class range, but both sources are classroom pages seen only in a search, and the typical cell in exploratorium-elodea (about 50 um long) is shorter than any drawn cell (77 um and up). Hold a drawn cell against the 50 um bar and compare it with a real Elodea slide.

code.sets: cell lengths 92 to 150 px = 77 to 125 um, end walls staggered and slanted

facts.fact: Cell files 36 px = 30 um; walls about 2 um as one bright line
facts.real: Two primary walls and the middle lamella read as one thin bright line, often about 1 um or less at 400x
facts.reason: The wall line is drawn 2.5 px (about 2 um) so it stays visible at phone width; a real wall line usually looks thinner.

code.sets: cell files 36 px = 30 um wide; walls drawn 2.5 px, about 2 um, as one bright line

facts.fact: 56 chloroplasts per cell
facts.real: Elodea cells are packed with chloroplasts (about 40 to 60 visible per cell)

code.sets: 56 chloroplasts per cell: 24 along the walls, 12 just inside, 20 over the face

facts.real: A 400x camera crop

views.view: Tonicity: Elodea leaf cells under the light microscope

open.steps: Tonicity and Osmosis Sandbox: tap "Plant cell (rigid wall)", then set External solute to 20.

views.depicts: Protoplasts pressed flat against the walls, no gaps at the corners, chloroplasts pressed along the walls. The wall holds the shape.
views.mustMatch: Wet mount of an Elodea leaf in pond or distilled water, brightfield, 400x.

facts.fact: Protoplast fills the cell to the wall (no corner gaps)
facts.real: Turgid cells show no gap at the wall

facts.fact: Cell outline unchanged from isotonic
facts.real: The wall stops the cell from swelling

code.sets: cell files 36 px = 30 um wide; walls drawn 2.5 px, about 2 um, as one bright line

simplified: Turgid and flaccid cells look much alike in real life too; the difference is the corner gaps.

views.view: Tonicity: Elodea leaf cells under the light microscope

open.steps: Tonicity and Osmosis Sandbox: tap "Plant cell (rigid wall)", then set External solute to 92.

views.depicts: Uneven plasmolysis: protoplasts round up and pull off the end walls first, by different amounts in different cells, chloroplasts crowd into a dense green mass, thin Hechtian strands still hold the membrane to the wall, two cells in eight go concave.
views.mustMatch: Wet mount of an Elodea leaf in strong salt solution (for example 5 to 10 percent NaCl), brightfield, 400x.

facts.fact: Named plasmolysis only above external solute 80
facts.real: Plasmolysis in a clearly hypertonic solution

facts.fact: Pull-in p = 0.43 + 0.57 x (external solute - 80) / 20: 0.46 at 81, 1 at 100
facts.real: Stronger solutions plasmolyze further

code.sets: how far protoplasts pull in

facts.fact: Per-cell factors 0.7 to 1.2, so plasmolysis is uneven
facts.real: Plasmolysis varies from cell to cell

code.sets: per-cell factors

facts.fact: Hechtian strands drawn only once plasmolyzed, three per cell
facts.real: Fine threads hold the pulled-away membrane to the wall

code.sets: strands

facts.fact: Still 56 chloroplasts per cell, so they crowd
facts.real: Chloroplasts pack together as the protoplast shrinks

code.sets: 56 chloroplasts per cell: 24 along the walls, 12 just inside, 20 over the face

views.view: Bone Layers: long bone cut lengthwise
views.state: all six stops (periosteum, compact bone, osteon, endosteum, spongy bone, medullary cavity)

open.steps: Body Systems Lab, Bone Layers tab: set the slider to stop 1 to 6 (drag through every stop).

views.depicts: An adult long bone cut lengthwise, marrow as in an adult femur: spongy bone filling the epiphyses and metaphyses under a thin shell and opening into the medullary cavity, a thick compact wall along the shaft, closed epiphyseal lines across the spongy bone, red marrow at the upper end and yellow marrow in the shaft and lower end.
views.mustMatch: Gross longitudinal section of an adult long bone (femur), as in a textbook photograph or a dry bone cut lengthwise.

facts.fact: Shaft wall 12 px thick on each side of a 54 px shaft (each wall about 22 percent of the shaft width); cavity 30 px
facts.real: Mid-shaft cortex about 5 to 7 mm in a femur about 25 to 30 mm across

code.match: the shaft wall: 12 px thick from x 111 to 249, tapering to the 2\.5 px end shell at x 84 and 276
code.sets: wall thickness and taper

facts.fact: End shell 2.5 px (21 percent of the shaft wall)
facts.real: The cortex over the ends is a thin shell, roughly 15 to 20 percent of the mid-shaft cortex (it varies along the end)
facts.reason: Just over the rough range given; if anything the real shell over the joint end is thinner.

code.sets: end shell (5 px stroke clipped to the bone: 2.5 px shows)

facts.fact: Diaphysis x 84 to 276 of a bone x 10 to 349 (57 percent of the length)
facts.real: Shaft about 60 to 75 percent of a long bone
facts.reason: A little short (57 against at least 60 percent): the simplified caps stand in for the epiphysis and the flared metaphysis and are drawn long. The bone is also stubbier than a femur overall (see simplified).

code.sets: cortex outline

facts.fact: 22 main trabeculae per end along stress lines, with cross-ties
facts.real: Trabeculae run in arches along stress lines, thicker near the joint

code.sets: strut count

facts.fact: Epiphyseal lines cross the spongy bone from shell to shell
facts.real: A dense plate across the end, trabeculae on both sides

code.sets: epiphyseal lines

facts.fact: Red marrow at the upper end, yellow in the shaft, mostly yellow at the lower end
facts.real: In adults red marrow stays mainly in the upper ends of the femur and humerus

code.sets: marrow gradient

simplified: No absolute scale: length to shaft width is about 6 to 1 (an adult femur is about 15 to 1).
The ends are simplified caps: no femoral head, neck or trochanters, so the label says "like adult femur".

views.view: Bone Layers: zoom, ground section of compact bone cut across
views.state: stop 3 (Osteon, zoom) at full strength; dimmed on the other stops

open.steps: Body Systems Lab, Bone Layers tab: set the slider to stop 3 (Osteon (zoom)).

views.depicts: A ground section of the shaft wall cut across: outer circumferential lamellae under the surface (periosteum removed), packed osteons (two older ones cut off by newer ones) with interstitial lamellae between them, dark empty Haversian canals, lacunae with dark canaliculi like small spiders, Volkmann canals from the surface and from canal to canal.
views.mustMatch: Ground (undecalcified, unstained) cross section of human compact bone, brightfield, about 40 to 100x.

facts.fact: Canal radius 0.2 of the osteon radius
facts.real: Haversian canal about 50 um in an osteon about 200 to 300 um across (0.17 to 0.25)

code.sets: canal size

facts.fact: 13 osteons, radius 26 to 36 px, most touching, four squashed about 10 percent
facts.real: Osteons pack tightly and many are oval

code.sets: osteon layout

facts.fact: 8 lamellae per osteon
facts.real: Usually 4 to 20 concentric lamellae

code.match: for \(var k = 1; k <= 7; k\+\+\) lam \+= circleD

facts.fact: 35 lacunae per osteon on four rings (5, 7, 10, 13)
facts.real: Lacunae sit between lamellae in several rings, more in the outer rings

code.sets: lacuna rings

facts.fact: Twelve canaliculi per lacuna, 4 to 9 px each; the inner ring reaches the canal
facts.real: A dense dark halo of canaliculi running mostly out from the canal

code.sets: canaliculus lengths

facts.fact: Six outer circumferential lamellae, 3.5 px apart
facts.real: A band of lamellae parallel to the surface under the periosteum

code.sets: circumferential lamellae

facts.fact: Canals and lacunae dark (#1e1612), no vessels drawn
facts.real: A ground section has no soft tissue: canals and lacunae look dark

facts.fact: Volkmann canals from the surface and from one Haversian canal to the next
